basis: Staphylococcal toxin-mediated infection umbrella; skin, pulmonary and systemic damage vary by subtype.
Lysosomal trafficking disorder with defining skeletal dysplasia and joint restriction; cardiac valvular disease occurs in >30% across the spectrum.
Defined by eyelid malformations and premature ovarian endocrine failure.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; scoliosis in 3/5 and hip dislocation in 2/4 support skeletal involvement; astigmatism in 2/4 supports ocular dysfunction.
Defining developmental impairment, congenital/developmental cataracts and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; digital contracture frequency uncertain beyond one reported patient.
Demyelinating neuropathy; muscle atrophy and pes cavus occur in 30-79%. Deafness is reported in severe variants, without established >=30% frequency across the subtype.
Defined by external ear and mandibular malformations; micrognathia/retrognathia in 4/9. Hearing loss and airway abnormalities each occur in a minority.
KCNQ3-related neonatal epilepsy; no established common damage outside the nervous system.
Inherited focal epilepsy with pericentral epileptiform activity.
Chronic intestinal motility failure defines the disease; neurologic and renal abnormalities are occasional (5-29%).
Malignant neoplasm located in the thalamus; endocrine involvement is not established for the concept itself.
Developmental delay and cardiac malformations are in the definition; strabismus occurs in 30-79%. Minor ear and digit dysmorphisms do not establish functional damage.
B-cell lymphoma defined by small-vessel occupation; CNS dysfunction occurs in ~30-40%. Skin and liver involvement vary geographically and are omitted under the four-axis cap.
Intellectual disability, movement disorder, deafness and ophthalmoplegia define the syndrome; skeletal contractures and renal anomalies are occasional.
Complex hereditary spastic paraplegia; hearing impairment and cataracts each occur in 30-79%.
SET-related intellectual disability with universal reported developmental delay; additional organ abnormalities are individually below 30%.
Progressive visual loss, scoliosis/kyphoscoliosis and arachnodactyly define the syndrome.
Defined by intracranial arterial disease and achalasia; ischemic stroke with hemiparesis in 4/9 establishes common direct brain injury.
Developmental impairment is common across chromosome 6 deletion syndromes; other organ malformations depend on the deleted region and lack a shared >=30% frequency.
Keratinizing lesion of the middle ear with local destructive growth; preceding infections do not make the lesion itself an infection.
Inherited HDL/apolipoprotein disorder; coronary atherosclerosis (2/5) is a separate disease. Ocular findings and tendon xanthomas are each reported in only 1/5.
Spectrum principally includes tubulointerstitial kidney disease and primary antibody deficiency; severe congenital neutropenia is a minority presentation.
Defining fetal akinesia and congenital joint contractures; skeletal muscle atrophy in 3/5. No established common pulmonary or independent neurologic injury is supplied.
Menstrual pain due to pelvic reproductive pathology; no organ within the 13 axes is intrinsically affected.
Anophthalmia and esophageal atresia define the reported syndrome; cryptorchidism is reproductive and does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
